hints: Multiply both sides by $(x - 1)$ to clear the algebraic fraction: $(3x + 2)(x - 1) = 2$.
Expand and rearrange into standard quadratic form $3x^2 - x - 4 = 0$.
Factorise $(3x - 4)(x + 1) = 0$ to find both values of $x$.
walkthrough:
Multiply both sides of the equation by $(x - 1)$ to clear the denominator:
$$(3x + 2)(x - 1) = 2$$

Expand the brackets and collect all terms on one side:
$$3x^2 - 3x + 2x - 2 = 2 \implies 3x^2 - x - 4 = 0$$
